options: A replacement for DevOps that removes the operations role
A security audit performed after every production release
DevOps with the addition of a security step
A framework for encrypting data pipelines
A methodology that replaces Agile with security reviews
questions.explanation: DevSecOps is nothing less than DevOps, but with an additional step for security.

questions.stem: What do the three parts of the name DevSecOps stand for?
options: Development, Security and Operations
Device, Section and Optimisation
Development, Secrecy and Output
Deployment, Secure and Observation
Design, Security and Orchestration
questions.explanation: DevSecOps stands for development, security and operations.

questions.stem: Why has security become an alarming factor in DevOps?
options: Because DevOps teams no longer use version control
Because operations teams were removed from projects
Because Agile forbids security testing
Because DevOps relies on mainframe infrastructure
Because of the quick and fast deployment cycles
questions.explanation: The speed of DevOps deployment cycles made security an alarming concern, which led to DevSecOps.

questions.stem: At what point in the DevOps flow has security been included to form DevSecOps?
options: After production release
Right before the creation process
Only during monitoring
After packaging but before release
During version control only
questions.explanation: Security has been included right before the creation process, and that is how DevSecOps came onto the surface.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the DevSecOps name?
options: Development
Security
Operations
Data
Sec, meaning security
questions.explanation: DevSecOps combines development, security and operations; data is not part of the name.

questions.stem: How does DevSecOps relate to DevOps?
options: It is a smaller subset of DevOps practices
It is unrelated to DevOps
It replaces DevOps automation with manual checks
It is nothing less than DevOps, plus security
It removes the operations step from DevOps
questions.explanation: DevSecOps keeps everything DevOps has and adds security as an extra step.

questions.stem: Which factor caused DevSecOps to come onto the surface?
options: The rise of Big Data file formats
Security concerns arising from fast DevOps deployment cycles
The need to reduce data liabilities
The introduction of machine learning models
Regulations requiring separate operations teams
questions.explanation: DevSecOps emerged because the quick deployment cycles of DevOps made security an alarming factor.

questions.stem: In the abbreviation DevSecOps, what does "Sec" refer to?
options: Second-stage testing
Sector operations
Secondary deployment
Section management
Security
questions.explanation: "Sec" stands for security, the step added to DevOps to form DevSecOps.

questions.stem: Which statement about DevSecOps is correct?
options: It keeps the DevOps steps and adds security before the creation process
It applies security only after software reaches production
It slows deployment cycles deliberately to improve safety
It replaces automated deployment with manual security sign-off
It is concerned with data pipelines rather than software
questions.explanation: DevSecOps is DevOps with security added right before the creation process.

questions.stem: Which statement about DevSecOps is NOT true?
options: It adds a security step to DevOps
It arose because fast deployment cycles made security alarming
It removes the operations step from DevOps
Its name combines development, security and operations
It includes security right before the creation process
questions.explanation: DevSecOps does not remove anything from DevOps; it adds security to the existing development and operations practices.
